sections.heading: Problem
paragraphs: Per the file, messages transmitted to Solana nodes must not exceed the (per the file) IPv6 MTU size to (per the file) ensure fast and reliable (per the file) network transmission of cluster info over UDP. Per the file, solana's networking stack uses (per the file) a conservative MTU size of (per the file) 1280 bytes which, after accounting (per the file) for headers, leaves 1232 bytes (per the file) for packet data like serialized txs. Per the file, developers building applications on (per the file) Solana must design their (per the file) on-chain program interfaces within the above tx size limit constraint. Per the file, one common work-around is (per the file) to store state temporarily on-chain (per the file) and consume that state in later txs. Per the file, this is the approach (per the file) used by the BPF (per the file) loader program for deploying Solana programs.

Per the file, however, this workaround doesn't (per the file) work well when developers compose (per the file) many on-chain programs in a (per the file) single atomic tx. Per the file, with more composition comes more acct inputs, each of which (per the file) takes up 32 bytes. Per the file, there is currently no (per the file) available workaround for increasing the number of accts used in a single tx since each tx must list all accts that it needs to properly lock accts for parallel execution. Per the file, therefore the current cap is about 35 accts after accounting for signatures and other tx metadata.
